 This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the dismissal of the claim petition in MVC No.53/2011, dated 28.01.2012.
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.14,60,000/- for the death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.
2. The case of the claimant is that the deceased was working as cleaner of the lorry belonging to the first respondent.
On 17.01.2010 he was going in the lorry in NC: 2023:KHC:37436 the capacity of loader and transporting sugarcane.

At about 11.30 a.m, in front of water tank in between Belavadi - Maduvadi road, live electricity wire was passing and as per the directions of the driver of the lorry,
the deceased tried to lift the live electricity wire with the hello of a stick, but unfortunately he was electrocuted and died at the spot itself.

The legal representatives of the deceased have filed a statement stating that the instructions of the driver of the vehicle and because of this negligence he had lift the electricity wire and he was electrocuted.
It is submitted that there is negligence they are entitled for compensation.
The Tribunal had dismissed the claim petition observing that PW1 is the wife of the deceased is not an eye-witness.

PW2 is the one who has filed examination in chief narrating how the accident had occurred and in the cross-examination of PW2 he had deposed that,
the deceased tried to push the loaded lorry, the wire came in contact with the lorry and he fell down and died an account of electric shock.
The Court below had observed the evidence of PW2 who is only the eye- NC: 2023:KHC:37436 witness.
It is not the case of the claimants that the deceased on the instruction of the driver tried to lift the live electricity wire and he died.

The Court below had also observed that there was no evidence on record to show that the deceased was working in this Smt Mallajamma vs Sri Channamallaiah on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94334989/
2 particular vehicle as a loader.

Without the said evidence and also the negligence on the part of the driver, they are not entitled for any claim under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act and accordingly dismissed the claim petition.
3. On 11.10.2023, there was no representation on behalf of the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent is present.
Hence, this Court directed the matter to be listed under the caption for dismissal.
Today also when the matter is called, there was no representation on behalf of the appellant.
As this is an appeal of 2012, this Court is not inclined to adjourn the matter.

This Court is proceeding with the matter basing on the material available on record, in support of the grounds of the appeal it is stated that the Court had failed to NC: 2023:KHC:37436 appreciate the evidence available on record and the reasons for the dismissal are unsustainable.
The Court relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of the National Insurance Company Limited V/s Prembai Patel and another1

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Prembai Patel and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the claimants are at liberty to file claim petition, either on the Motor Vehicles Act or workman Compensation Act.
While assessing the compensation the Tribunal should have adopted the principles enumerated under the Workman Compensation Act.
It is stated that the Court below without appreciating the evidence had dismissed the claim petition.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal had rightly dismissed the petition and whether they can maintain an application under Section 166 of the Act or under the Workman Compensation Act is not the issue.

It is submitted that while an application is filed under Section 166 of Motor 2005(6) SCC 172 NC: 2023:KHC:37436 Vehicles Act, the burden lies on the claimants to prove that there is negligence, whereas in this case as he has failed to prove the negligence, the Court below had rightly dismissed the claim petition.
5. Having heard the learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company this Court has perused the entire material on record.
According to the claimants, because of the negligence on the part of the driver, the deceased has touched the live wire and he died.
PW1 is the wife of the deceased who is not an eye-witness and PW2 is the eye-witness.
According to him, the deceased tried to push the loaded lorry the live electricity wire came in contact with the lorry and he fell down which is a different version from that of the claimant.

The Court below had rightly observed that when an application is filed under Section 166 of the Act, they have to prove the negligence and unless the negligence is proved they are not entitled for any relief.
Admittedly, in this case the claimants failed to prove that there is negligence on the NC: 2023:KHC:37436 part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
In that view of the matter this Court finds no reasons to interfere.

6. Accordingly the appeal of the claimant is dismissed.
i) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
ii) No costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
